report_label: NOT CLINICAL VALIDATION -- technical evaluation on 12 AI-written synthetic, unreviewed cases.
purpose: Case file for the Control vs A0 clinical evaluation. The 12 cases currently here are the pre-existing AI-written synthetic notes from scripts/verify_malayalam_manglish.py and scripts/verify_malayalam_manglish_stress.py, copied verbatim as a TECHNICAL PILOT ONLY. They are marked synthetic_unreviewed and must never be presented as clinical validation. Clinician-reviewed, de-identified cases are to be added here.

conventions.expected_grams: TOTAL prescribed/dispensed grams per herb, not per-dose grams.
conventions.frequency_and_duration: Not represented by ClinicalParse; never inferred or graded.
conventions.expected_dosha: Set of canonical doshas (Vata, Pitta, Kapha); order-insensitive, compared as sets.
conventions.expected_herbs: Canonical clinic herb name -> {grams, tolerance_grams}; tolerance is absolute grams, default 0.
conventions.null_expected_field: Allowed only when ambiguous=true; that field is not auto-graded.
conventions.mentioned_not_stocked: Herb names in the note that the clinic does not stock; proposing any of them is flagged.
conventions.safety_annotations: Clinician-supplied only (source must be 'clinician', annotated_by required). The grader evaluates them mechanically and never adds rules of its own. Types: herb_must_not_be_proposed {herb}, herb_max_total_grams {herb, max_grams}, requires_clinician_review {description}.

cases.label: Non-stocked herb mentioned alongside a real one

provenance.origin: AI-written synthetic note (technical pilot only; not clinical ground truth)
provenance.source_label: Non-stocked herb mentioned alongside a real one

cases.notes: vata kൂടുതൽ. thulasi ela kurachu kodukkanam, koode ashwagandha 20 gram.
cases.source_rationale: Thulasi (Tulsi) is deliberately NOT one of this clinic's stocked herbs (the formulary grew from 8 to 20 herbs in Sep 2026, and Tulsi was a candidate that was left out on purpose, specifically so this test would stay meaningful) and has no alias entry at all. Per the tightened prompt, Gemini should leave it out entirely rather than guess a canonical name for it -- expected output has ONLY Ashwagandha. If Tulsi shows up in the output under any name, that's the 'guessing past an unknown herb' failure mode this test exists to catch.

cases.label: Imprecise quantity (genuinely ambiguous)

provenance.origin: AI-written synthetic note (technical pilot only; not clinical ground truth)

cases.notes: vata pitta mix. ashwagandha kurachu koodutham venam, 20-25 g range il. brahmi original dose 15.
cases.ambiguity_reason: '20-25 g range' has no single correct integer -- this system requires a strict integer gram count, so there is no objectively right answer here. Read the actual output and judge whether Gemini's choice (or refusal) is reasonable; this case is NOT auto-graded.
